title: Lightning plugin onramp — playsmith notes
content:
Goal: give a 5–15 minute, runnable path for engineers to add a Redwood plugin (local dev -> sandbox -> production toggle) that demonstrates: local zero-config dev, automatic telemetry, opt-in sidecar vs embedded adapter, and rollback safety. This is intentionally compact and action-oriented — keep it as a lab doc for pairing sessions and demos.

Motivation / context:
- Many teams want to extend Redwood SDKs with small feature plugins (auth adapters, prompt formatters, result post-processors, reranker hooks). Existing quickstarts focus on full SDK boot but not tiny plugin flows.
- This doc is a lightweight lab: ship a plugin, run tests locally, flip a runtime feature flag to promote it to sandbox/dedicated routes.

High-level flow (10–15 min):
1) scaffold plugin with CLI (2 min)
2) run local mock server and adapter (2–3 min)
3) exercise integration with a tiny sample app and telemetry (3–5 min)
4) flip to sandbox route via config and smoke test (2–3 min)

Step 0 — prerequisites:
- Node 18+ or Python 3.11 installed (examples provided in both languages)
- local redwood-devkit: npm i -g @redwood/devkit (or pip install redwood-devkit)
- git, curl, and Docker optional for sidecar emulation

Step 1 — scaffold (CLI)
- Command: redwood devkit plugin new --name playsmith --lang js --template minimal
- What this produces: package.json, src/index.js (entry), manifest.yaml, tests/basic.spec.js, README.md
- manifest.yaml fields to glance at: id, version, compatibility (sdk_version_range), mode: embedded|sidecar

Step 2 — local mock runtime
- Start a local runtime simulator that exposes the same HTTP surface as Redwood routes: redwood devkit runtime --listen 127.0.0.1:8088 --mock
- In embedded mode the SDK loads plugin code directly. In sidecar mode the plugin runs in its own process and communicates over HTTP gRPC (this simulates Private/Dedicated separation).
- Example minimal plugin (src/index.js):
  module.exports = async function handle(requestContext, next) {
    // simple prompt annotation
    requestContext.prompt = `[play:annotated] ${requestContext.prompt}`;
    const res = await next(requestContext);
    // attach a debugging tag to telemetry envelope
    res.meta = {...res.meta, playsmith: true};
    return res;
  }
- Run locally: npm run dev (the scaffold includes a dev script that watches and reloads)

Step 3 — sample app exercise
- Checkout tiny sample app: git clone https://github.com/redwood-inference/playsmith-samples && cd playsmith-samples
- Set REDWOOD_RUNTIME=https://127.0.0.1:8088 in .env or export env var
- Run sample: npm start
- Send a quick request: curl -X POST $REDWOOD_RUNTIME/generate -d '{"prompt":"Summarize the onboarding plan"}' -H 'Content-Type: application/json'
- Observe plugin behavior: the returned text will include annotation and telemetry logs in runtime console.

Telemetry / observability defaults:
- The scaffold emits a telemetry envelope to local dev console that mirrors production shape: trace_id, plugin_id, duration_ms, tags.
- Telemetry is off by default in dev; enable via REDWOOD_TELEMETRY=1 to see sample events posted to local sink: http://127.0.0.1:4318 (OTLP collector stub).
- Recommended minimal telemetry fields for plugins: plugin.id, plugin.version, hook.name (pre|post), duration_ms, error:bool, sample_rate

Step 4 — sandbox promotion (config toggle)
- Patch the route config in sandbox: curl -X PATCH https://console.sandbox.redwood.internal/api/routes/mini-play -H 'Authorization: Bearer <token>' -d '{"plugin_chain": ["playsmith@v0.1.0"]}'
- Or use the local devkit command to stage: redwood devkit promote --route mini-play --plugin playsmith@v0.1.0 --env sandbox
- Smoke test: send test traffic through the sandboxed endpoint (curl to sandbox route). Monitor route-level latency and plugin traces in the Redwood Console.

Safety: rollback and automatic fallback
- The runtime includes a plugin watchdog that enforces a 250ms hook timeout by default. If a plugin exceeds the timeout, runtime skips the plugin's result and logs a warning to traces.
- Canary traffic: promote to sandbox with 1% traffic weight first; observe metrics for 10–30 minutes. Use console rollout controls to increment.

Developer ergonomics notes (why these defaults):
- zero-config local runtime with mock sink reduces onboarding friction — no infra prerequisites to validate wiring.
- manifest.yaml provides a clear compatibility contract so we can warn at dev-time if SDK/runtime mismatch.
- sidecar vs embedded mode: sidecar isolates memory/CPU usage (recommended for heavy post-processing), embedded is faster for tiny hooks.

Common troubleshooting (quick checklist):
- plugin not loading: check manifest.id matches package.json name; devkit watches manifest changes only on save.
- no telemetry events: ensure REDWOOD_TELEMETRY=1 and check that OTLP stub is reachable.
- request hangs: enable PLUGIN_DEBUG=1 to get per-hook timing. If sidecar, confirm Docker container port mapping.
- sandbox route not using plugin: confirm route config includes plugin_chain and that plugin version exists in the sandbox artifact store.

Testing guidance (automated):
- basic unit test included: tests/basic.spec.js asserts transform and metadata attach. Run: npm test
- runtime integration test: redwood devkit runtime --mock && npm run test:integration (this runs the sample app against the local runtime)
- CI: publish plugin artifact to internal registry and run a smoke job that hits a dedicated sandbox route and asserts response contains playsmith tag.

Security & compliance reminders:
- Plugins are treated as customer-supplied code. For public/shared routes, require review and sign-off.
- Manifest must declare data-plane access levels (read-only prompts, read-write KV cache, network access). Default to minimal privileges.

Next steps / follow-ups (TODOs):
- Create a short 3–slide deck and 2min recorded demo for handbook. (owner: Marco)
- Add Python example for plugin skeleton (owner: Jin)
- Add one-click Console button that installs plugin into a sandbox route from the devkit manifest (explore API surface).
- Draft a small security checklist for plugin reviewers (SLO: 1 page).

Notes to self / lab hints:
- During pairing sessions, start in embedded mode then flip to sidecar to show isolation benefits.
- Keep the first demo prompt small to highlight annotation behaviour.
- Use sample telemetry to show how to filter traces by plugin.id in Console.

Appendix — manifest.yaml example (minimal):
  id: playsmith
  version: 0.1.0
  sdk_range: ">=1.8.0 <2.0.0"
  mode: embedded
  entry: src/index.js
  permissions:
    - type: prompt_read
    - type: telemetry_write

Appendix — quick curl to test sidecar health: curl http://127.0.0.1:9090/healthz

If you want, I can convert this into a 1-page printable quickstart and a step-by-step slide deck for the onboarding workshop.
